summary: Revised plan adds the customer_note column idempotently via ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS in the expand stage, ensuring the column exists before the Django migration runs during deploy_new. A backfill step populates existing rows, and the contract stage removes the old note column after the new version is confirmed running. This eliminates the duplicate-column error and maintains concurrent-read/write consistency.
write_consistency: During concurrent operation, the old app writes to note, the new app writes to customer_note. The expand stage ensures all existing rows have a customer_note value inherited from note. After deploy_new, only the new app writes to customer_note; after retire_old, the note column is dropped. Reads from either version see the most recent write to their respective column, and the backfill guarantees no note data is lost during the transition.
revision_notes: Root cause: the original expand_1 added customer_note, but the subsequent deploy_new Django migration issued ADD COLUMN customer_note, which failed with ProgrammingError: column already exists because the column was already present. Fix: use ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS in the expand SQL stage so the column creation is idempotent, and sequence the stages so the Django migration runs after the column exists. A backfill step ensures existing note values are preserved in the new column.

stages.description: Add the customer_note column idempotently so the Django migration in deploy_new does not fail.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS customer_note TEXT NULL;

stages.description: Back-fill existing note values into customer_note so no data is lost before the old app is retired.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE customer_note IS NULL AND note IS NOT NULL;

stages.description: Deploy the new-staged version of Saleor. The Django migration is state-only and expects customer_note to already exist (provided by expand_1).
Shut down the old version of Saleor. No further writes or reads against the note column will occur from the old code after this point.
Remove the now-unused note column from the account_user table.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
